prompt:
You are a "goldfish" reviewer: a fresh reader with no history of this project. You are strictly read-only: do not edit, write or create any file, and do not run git commands that change anything.

The project is theOS, a standalone, fresh project in /home/user/maiacity/theOS/. Everything is built from scratch inside theOS/. Code outside theOS/ (maiacity, aven/DB2, aven/ops, the repository's .claude and CLAUDE.md) is legacy: it may be learned from, never changed or depended on. theOS now owns avenSANDBOX and the release pipeline (AIP-2): taking them over is AIP-2's work, nothing else changes legacy code. Do not propose reusing legacy code by import or by editing it.

theOS keeps one JSON doc per thing, each with a "type", linking others by path: a path like "aip/AIP-1" is the file theOS/aip/AIP-1.json.

Read this record, plus the docs and files it names:
  /home/user/maiacity/theOS/aip/AIP-2.json
It is one intent of avenCEO, theOS's agent harness. avenCEO's definition is theOS/avenCEO/avenCEO.json; read it and the step, gate and type docs it links.

Earlier review rounds are the review docs listed under the record's "reviews", each with an answer to every finding. Those findings are settled: do not raise them again unless the record shows the fix did not actually happen. The record's "events" are append-only history: older events may describe earlier revisions; judge the record as it stands now.

Your job is the comprehension test.
1. First, in your own words, write two short paragraphs (2 to 5 sentences each) under these exact headings:
   **What this proposes**
   **How the existing system works, per this record**
   If you cannot paraphrase a part, say so: that is itself a Blocker finding.
2. Then list findings. Each finding: Severity (Blocker | Major | Nit), the affected part (field name or claim id), and what is unclear, undefined, assumed without saying, or contradictory. Look especially for: terms specific to this project that are never defined (general software terms are fine); places that assume knowledge a newcomer would not have; claims whose check would not actually catch the stated failure; contradictions between the record and avenCEO's definition.

Report in plain text, at most 500 words. No praise, no filler: lead with what is wrong or missing. If you find no Blocker or Major, say so plainly.

paraphrase.proposes: theOS takes over, from legacy avenDB, both the cloud session's sandbox (a prebuilt container image plus a warm-up script) and the release pipeline. Checkpoint 1 is already done at Samuel's direct ask: avenDB's four workflows were moved out of .github/workflows/ so they stop running, and nothing live was touched. Checkpoint 2 builds theOS's own box image, using only theOS/sandbox/box/, tagged by input hash and running aip-31df's check command, plus a new environment setup script that never fails a session. Checkpoint 3 adds a release workflow on production that publishes dated versions only when something changed. Deploying to aven.maia.city, and adding Lean and Rust to the box, are deferred.
paraphrase.existing: Before the park, avensandbox.yml released avenOS, avenSANDBOX and avenPEER from production, which takes changes from main only, under dated versions. Two workflows built the box and peer images from aven/DB2, and avendeploy.yml deployed to aven.maia.city by hand. Each new session's setup script runs aven/DB2/sandbox/box/cloud-setup.sh, which warms avenDB's box with four peers, and exits 0 if that file is missing. I cannot say what "avenSANDBOX" names: the environment, the image, or a released package. It is used as all three.

findings.text: What theOS releases, and what a release is (tag, GitHub release, package), cannot be paraphrased. "Something it ships" depends on an unanswered question, yet c4 goes to Gate A.
findings.note: Revision 2: checkpoint 3 and c4 are deferred until you answer what theOS releases and where. Nothing goes to Gate A that depends on that answer.

findings.text: GitHub runs the workflow files of the branch being pushed. avensandbox-image.yml runs on a push to any branch, avenpeer-image.yml on any but production; every branch made before the park still has them, and production keeps avensandbox.yml until main is merged into it. "Once the park reaches main, none runs" is false, and reading the active-workflow list would not catch a run on another branch.
findings.note: c1 now says what is true: no avenDB workflow runs on main or production once the park reaches them; branches made before the park keep their copies until they merge main. Its check reads the Actions runs of main and production, not the list of workflows.

findings.text: production's ruleset (SANDBOX.md, Samuel's part 5) requires the checks "Only from main" and "avenSANDBOX", which only the parked avensandbox.yml reports: every PR into production already fails, so "a PR from another branch fails" passes even if theOS's workflow guards nothing. The record never mentions the ruleset. No positive case (a PR from main that changed something releases), and nothing checks the version format.
findings.note: The ruleset is named: production requires two checks only the parked workflow reported, so nothing merges into production until theOS releases. That is intended now (nothing releases); changing the ruleset is part of the deferred release.

findings.text: "High" is not one of aven's two levels (can be undone / can't be undone), and step 1's question "can it be undone?" is not answered. The rating covers only the park, though checkpoints 2 and 3 change every new session and the release path. No tested undo is named, though aven's Build step requires one for a release.
findings.note: Risk now uses avenCEO's levels: can be undone. The park by moving the files back; the setup script by switching the environment's script back.

findings.text: avenSANDBOX, box, warm, park, avenOS, avenPEER/Aven Peer and the production branch have no term docs.
findings.note: Term docs added: avenSANDBOX, Box, Warm, Park, avenOS, avenPEER, production.

findings.text: It needs aip-31df's check command, which aip-31df has not built, and the dependency is never stated. No check covers "tagged by the hash of its inputs". How a session gets the image (which tag, which registry package, public or not, the ghcr.io network allowance) is not said.
findings.note: Revision 2: the box is a setup script, not an image, so no tag and no registry; c2 waits for aip-31df's checkpoint 1 (the check command), written as a dependency.

findings.text: "For you to paste", and probably making the package public, are human steps outside the two gates, against aven's "you are needed twice", and not listed as assumptions. Which branch gets the planted failure, which every new session would run, is not said. A hang passes "exits 0". Switching the script also drops avenDB's warm box, which d-ff11 allowed for testing.
findings.note: Pasting the environment's setup script is part of Gate B (you try it), so you are still needed twice. The planted failure runs in a copy, not on a branch; the script is wrapped in a time limit, so a hang exits 0 too. Cloud sessions keep their own Chromium, so dropping avenDB's warm box loses no check.

findings.text: It cites "question 2" for what theOS serves; that is question 3. Question 3's recommended answer (deploy once checkpoint 3 is green) has no checkpoint or claim.
findings.note: The deferred item names the question by its words, not a number.

findings.text: How aven.maia.city reports "26.10.31v6" is not said; the evidence shows it was released, not deployed. When and by whom the park reaches main is not said, yet c1 and checkpoint 2 wait on it.
findings.note: c1's check reads aven.maia.city's answer (it answers) and the Actions runs; the park reaches main with this branch's merge, which you ask for.

findings.text: "Every release and box image comes from files in theOS/" contradicts truth 5 (workflow files live outside theOS/). A release's tag cannot show where its files came from.
findings.note: The outcome is now the cost a person feels: a new session reaches a green theOS check with no avenDB warm-up.

findings.text: aven's Gate A also covers the assumptions and the mockup, and offers "send back"; the question offers only Yes or Change.
findings.note: Gate A's question now covers the claims, assumptions, outcome and mockup, and offers send back.

findings.text: The park's event writes nothing although it moved four files and edited CLAUDE.md, and names no commit.
findings.note: writes lists brain's docs only; the moved files are outside brain. A new event names the park's commit, 2d6f53842.
